That precision is exactly what makes it dangerous to act on unexamined. Its own text names the mechanism as price-sensitive buyers, and it reports new accounts and booked revenue but says nothing about retention, expansion, or realized revenue beyond the promo window. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, discount-led acquisition of price-sensitive accounts is a known pattern for inflating short-horizon metrics while degrading cohort quality; matching a competitor on price also invites a margin race we have no evidence we win. I want the source record to see the measurement horizon and whether retention was tracked at all before that memory is allowed to steer a slot that does not carry over. Referral incentives (memory_57) depend on established customers activating well, which is precisely what is currently degrading, so it is downstream of the fix rather than a substitute for it. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if verification undercuts memory_86, since it targets the activation drop directly, though it treats a symptom lower in the funnel. Scale is a standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the supporting evidence is aged and was gathered under different competitive conditions, so I want a measured read with cohort-quality guardrails (not just completion rate, but downstream activation and retained qualified revenue) before committing further. If verification shows memory_86's lift was measured only on completion with no durable adoption follow-through, I will narrow to a small guarded test.
